bib.title: A-RAG: Scaling Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Hierarchical Retrieval Interfaces

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "A-RAG: Scaling Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Hierarchical Retrieval Interfaces", Mingxuan Du, Benfeng Xu, Chiwei Zhu, Shaohan Wang, Pengyu Wang, Xiaorui Wang, Zhendong Mao (USTC; Metastone). Preprint, arXiv:2602.03442v1, 3-4 Feb 2026. Footer: "Preprint. Work in progress."

COVERAGE: All 51,364 chars read, including limitations and appendices A-E. References were only skimmed. The text is clean. I did not run the figures script, because captions are in the extraction.

FIT WARNING: This paper does not mention PRINCE, Bayer, Text-to-SQL, metadata filters, query expansion, rerankers or hybrid search. It is about A-RAG, an agentic RAG framework on open-domain multi-hop QA. Note 08 (read in full) covers PRINCE and cites Kulkarni 2026, Search-o1 (arXiv:2501.05366) and Singh et al. (arXiv:2501.09136). This paper is not among those. It could only sharpen the "When agentic RAG pays" section or the "tools multiply" section, as an independent data point. The call is yours.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A-RAG (Full), with keyword_search, semantic_search and chunk_read exposed to a ReAct-style agent, beats the Naive RAG, Graph-RAG and Workflow-RAG baselines on every benchmark with GPT-5-mini.
  number: MuSiQue 74.1 LLM-Acc vs Naive RAG 52.8; HotpotQA 94.5 vs 81.2; 2Wiki 89.7 vs 50.2; Med. 93.1 vs 86.1; Novel 85.3 vs 70.6.
  setup: GPT-5-mini backbone. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, top-k=5 for all baselines. GPT-5-mini is the judge. Baselines reproduced locally. Four datasets: MuSiQue, HotpotQA, 2Wiki and GraphRAG-Bench (Med., Novel).
  quote: "A-RAG (Full) 74.1 65.3 94.5 88.0 89.7 88.9 93.1 85.3" and "Naive RAG 52.8 48.7 81.2 79.5 50.2 66.5 86.1 70.6"
  where: Table 1, p.6
- claim: With GPT-4o-mini the win is weaker. A-RAG (Full) is best on 3 of 5 datasets, and HippoRAG2 beats it on HotpotQA and 2Wiki (80.7 and 64.7 LLM-Acc against A-RAG 77.1 and 60.2). Agentic gains depend on a strong reasoning/tool-use model.
  number: MuSiQue 46.1 vs Naive RAG 38.6
  setup: GPT-4o-mini backbone, same setup as above.
  quote: "With GPT-4o-mini as the backbone, A-RAG (Full) achieves the best performance on 3 out of 5 datasets."
  where: Sec 4.2, p.7; Table 1
- claim: Even the simplest agentic variant, A-RAG (Naive) with one embedding-search tool plus chunk_read, beats Naive RAG on all datasets. The gap is larger with GPT-5-mini.
  number: GPT-5-mini MuSiQue 66.2 vs 52.8; HotpotQA 90.8 vs 81.2
  setup: as above.
  quote: "A-RAG (Naive) surpasses existing Graph-RAG and Workflow RAG methods on multiple datasets, demonstrating the inherent advantages of the agentic paradigm."
  where: Sec 4.2, p.7
- claim: Plain vanilla retrieval is a robust baseline. Graph-RAG and workflow methods did not consistently beat Naive RAG under a unified setup. With GPT-4o-mini, GraphRAG scored 33.2 on HotpotQA against 74.5 for Naive RAG. With GPT-5-mini, MA-RAG scored 40.0 on MuSiQue against 52.8.
  number: see above
  setup: unified reproduction, top-k=5, max_tokens>=16384
  quote: "Existing Graph-RAG and Workflow RAG methods fail to consistently outperform these simple baselines across all datasets."
  where: Sec 4.2, p.7
- claim: Agentic retrieval can use fewer tokens than the baselines. A-RAG (Full) retrieves about the same or fewer tokens than Naive RAG on four of five datasets, while the single-tool A-RAG (Naive) retrieves 4-10x more.
  number: Full: MuSiQue 5,663, HotpotQA 2,737, 2Wiki 2,930, Med. 7,678, Novel 6,087. Naive RAG: 5,387 / 5,358 / 5,506 / 5,418 / 4,997. A-RAG (Naive): 56,360 / 27,455 / 45,406 / 23,657 / 22,391.
  setup: GPT-5-mini, tokens retrieved from the corpus
  quote: "A-RAG (Full) 5,6632,737 2,9307,678 6,087" and "A-RAG (Naive) 56,360 27,455 45,406 23,657 22,391"
  where: Table 3, p.8. The extraction runs the digits together; the figures are in the order given above. Note that Full retrieves more than Naive RAG on MuSiQue (5,663 vs 5,387), Med. and Novel, so "fewer" holds only for HotpotQA and 2Wiki.
- claim: Progressive disclosure (snippets first, then chunk_read) is the efficiency mechanism.
  number: none
  quote: "A-RAG (Naive) retrieves more tokens than A-RAG (Full) but achieves lower performance."
  where: Sec 5.2, p.8
- claim: Ablation. Removing semantic search hurts MuSiQue most (74.1 to 69.4 LLM-Acc). Removing keyword search costs 1.5 points on MuSiQue. Removing chunk_read costs 0.5 points on MuSiQue LLM-Acc (74.1 to 73.6) and slightly raises Cont-Acc (65.3 to 67.0). The other datasets move by 1 point or less. The paper's "Removing either ... leads to degradation" overstates this: on Novel, w/o KW is 93.2 vs 93.1 for Full, and on Med., w/o KW is +0.1.
  number: 69.4 vs 74.1
  setup: GPT-5-mini, Table 2
  quote: "w/o Semantic 69.4 63.3 93.9 88.4 89.1 88.0 92.1 85.2"
  where: Table 2, p.7
- claim: Test-time scaling. Raising max steps from 5 to 20 gives GPT-5-mini about +8% and GPT-4o-mini about +4%. Raising reasoning effort from minimal to high gives about +25% for both GPT-5-mini and GPT-5.
  number: ~8%, ~4%, ~25%
  setup: first 300 MuSiQue tasks only (MuSiQue-300). The extraction does not say whether the gains are absolute or relative.
  quote: "When scaling from 5 to 20 steps, GPT-5-mini improves by approximately 8% while GPT-4o-mini improves by only about 4%"
  where: Sec 5.1, p.8; Fig 4
- claim: The failure bottleneck shifts from retrieval to reasoning. About 50% of Naive RAG failures (GPT-4o-mini) are retrieval limits (multi-hop retrieval + top-k insufficient). A-RAG's dominant failure on MuSiQue is a reasoning chain error. Entity confusion is the largest sub-type.
  number: Naive RAG HotpotQA/MuSiQue: Model Understanding 36%/35%, Multi-hop Retrieval 27%/36%, Judge Error 23%/14%, Top-K Insufficient 13%/15%. A-RAG MuSiQue/2Wiki: Reasoning Chain Error 82%/45%, Model Gave Up 3%/33%, Judge Error 9%/19%, Corpus Missing 6%/3%. Within reasoning errors: Entity Confusion 40%/71%, Wrong Strategy 28%/29%, Question Misunderstanding 22%/0%, Exceed Budget 10%/0%.
  setup: first 100 incorrect cases, manually labelled. The settings differ: Naive RAG used GPT-4o-mini on HotpotQA and MuSiQue; A-RAG used GPT-5-mini on MuSiQue and 2Wiki. The two sets are not like-for-like.
  quote: "A-RAG's dominant failure mode (82% on MuSiQue) is reasoning chain errors, shifting the bottleneck to \"found documents but reasoned incorrectly\"."
  where: App D, pp.14-16; Tables 6-8
- claim: A-RAG satisfies all three authors' criteria for being "agentic": Autonomous Strategy, Iterative Execution and Interleaved Tool Use. MA-RAG and RAGentA are only partial.
  number: none
  quote: "A-RAG is the only method that fully satisfies all three, making it a truly agentic RAG framework."
  where: App A, Table 4, p.13
- claim: Design details. Chunks are about 1,000 tokens on sentence boundaries. Sentences are embedded and mapped back to the parent chunk, and a chunk's score is its best sentence. Keyword search uses no pre-index: exact match at query time, scored as sum of count*len(keyword). A context tracker returns "This chunk has been read before" at zero tokens. One tool call per step, no parallel calls.
  number: ~1,000 tokens/chunk; k=5 default, max 20
  quote: "Scorekw(ci,K) =X k∈K count(k, Ti)· |k|" and "chunks of approximately 1,000 tokens each"
  where: Sec 3, pp.4-5

LIMITS
- Authors concede (p.9): no systematic comparison of tool subsets; GPT-5 and Gemini-3 not tested in the main results ("computational resource constraints"); generalisation beyond multi-hop QA (fact verification, dialogue, long-form generation) is unverified.
- Not shown: no latency, wall-clock or dollar cost. Only retrieved tokens are reported, not the tokens the agent spends on reasoning and tool calls. No variance or seeds. The judge is GPT-5-mini, the same family as the backbone.
- The agent loop is deliberately minimal (ReAct, single tool call per step).
- All benchmarks are public Wikipedia-style multi-hop QA plus GraphRAG-Bench. There is no enterprise, structured/SQL, filtered or access-controlled data, so it says nothing about PRINCE-style stacks.
- "Work in progress" preprint. Scaling figures are on a 300-question subset.
- The main-text claim that GPT-5 would do better is untested ("we anticipate").

BUILDS ON (as printed): ReAct (Yao et al., 2023) for the loop. Chunking and corpora follow LinearRAG (Zhuang et al., 2025). Baselines: GraphRAG (Edge et al., 2025), HippoRAG2 (Gutiérrez et al., 2025a), FaithfulRAG (Zhang et al., 2025a), MA-RAG (Nguyen et al., 2025), RAGentA (Besrour et al., 2025). Contrasted with Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2023), FLARE (Jiang et al., 2023), IRCoT (Trivedi et al., 2023), RA-ISF (Liu et al., 2024), RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., 2024), LightRAG (Guo et al., 2025) and Lewis et al., 2021 (original RAG). Datasets: HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018), 2WikiMultiHopQA (Ho et al., 2020), MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., 2022), GraphRAG-Bench (Xiang et al., 2025). Embedder: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (Zhang et al., 2025b).

CODE: Algorithm 1 (A-RAG agent loop), App C, p.14, pseudocode only. Loop: for l=1..L, call the model with messages and tools. If it returns a tool call, execute it, append the result, and add chunk ids to C_read after chunk_read. Otherwise return the response. After L steps, append "Answer the question" and return M(M_msg). Tool descriptions (Figs 7-8, pp.17-18) carry load-bearing guidance. keyword_search: "Use SHORT, SPECIFIC terms (1-3 words maximum)". chunk_read: "you MUST use chunk_read to get the full content before formulating your answer". The system prompt for the full agent is "Work iteratively: search -> read -> evaluate -> search -> read -> ... -> answer." Code repo: https://github.com/Ayanami0730/arag (promised release).

FIGURES (from in-text captions; I did not render them)
- Fig 1, p.1: naive RAG vs agentic RAG paradigm and performance. Shows the autonomy difference.
- Fig 2, p.3: Graph RAG vs Workflow RAG vs Agentic RAG against the three autonomy principles.
- Fig 3, p.4: A-RAG overview, the agent iterating over keyword search, semantic search and chunk read. This is the fastest way to see the design.
- Fig 4, p.8: test-time scaling on MuSiQue-300, accuracy against max steps and against reasoning effort.
- Fig 5, p.8: failure-mode distribution.
- Fig 6: system prompts. Figs 7-8: tool descriptions.

- Table extraction merged some columns ("80.769.7", "5,6632,737", "93.9 88.4" order unverified for bold/underline marks). The numbers I quote are split from context, and the Table 3 splitting is inferred. Check against the PDF if a figure is used.
- Figure contents (the plots) were not read, only captions and surrounding text. The Fig 4 percentages are the authors' text.
